dedupe_keys.name: linda levee failure yuba river california 1986 lessons learned rogers and grote

description: This case study is the abstract of a paper by Rogers and Grote on the February 1986 levee break on the left bank of the Yuba River near its mouth with the Feather River in California. The breach flooded the towns of Linda and Olivehurst, inundating more than 4,000 homes and businesses, displacing more than 24,000 residents and causing over 400 million dollars in damage. It happened after the flood had crested, with the water 2.62 metres below the levee crest nine days after the storms began, and eyewitnesses described the landside toe softening and the embankment falling into a hole. Post-failure work built a historical database of the basin's levee generations, past failures, geomorphic processes and maintenance, and found that the first round of borings missed a highly conductive gravel cobble channel passing beneath the breach because it lay slightly deeper than the levee height, the limit set by Corps procedure. Coverage: one breach, with the full paper behind the abstract page. Access: the abstract page is free; the licence is not stated and the full text was not opened. Caveats: the record rests on the abstract only. It informs levee underseepage, foundation characterisation and breach-risk modelling, and relates to the ASDSO incident database in the catalogue.
